questions.prompt: What is your favourite subject at school?
questions.sampleA2:
I like history.

It is interesting and I like the stories.

It is sometimes boring but I like it.
questions.sampleB1:
My favourite subject is probably art.

I think it's really fun because you can be creative.

For example, I like painting and drawing.

However, it can be difficult sometimes if you don't have any ideas.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, my favourite subject has to be literature. I absolutely love how it lets you dive into different worlds and see life through someone else's eyes. I suppose what really draws me in is the way a good story can stick with you for years. The older texts can be a bit tricky to get your head around, but it's well worth the effort.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga tarix yoqadi.

U qiziqarli va menga hikoyalar yoqadi.

Ba'zan zerikarli bo'ladi, lekin menga yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Mening eng sevimli fanim, ehtimol, rasm chizishdir.

Menimcha, bu juda qiziqarli, chunki siz ijodkor bo'lishingiz mumkin.

Masalan, men rasm chizish va surat chizishni yaxshi ko'raman.

Biroq, agar sizda hech qanday g'oya bo'lmasa, ba'zan qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, eng sevimli fanim adabiyot bo'ladi.

Men turli nuqtai nazarlarni o'rganish va tilning nozik jihatlarini tushunishni juda qiziqarli deb bilaman.

O'qish menga qahramonlarga hamdard bo'lishga va muqobil nuqtai nazarlarni ko'rib chiqishga imkon beradi, bu menimcha juda qimmatli.

Garchi ba'zi eski matnlarni tushunish biroz qiyin bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, ularning inson tabiatiga oid beradigan tushunchalari harakatga arziydi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - What is your favourite subject at school?
sentenceStarters: "My favourite subject at school is definitely…" - "Maktabdagi eng sevimli fanimˌ albattaˌ…"
"I find it incredibly fascinating because…" - "Men buni juda qiziqarli deb bilaman, chunki…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
My favourite subject at school is definitely English. I find it incredibly fascinating because it opens doors to so many opportunities — from understanding foreign films to communicating with people around the world.
I also enjoy the creative side of it, like writing essays and learning new expressions. I believe having a strong command of English is essential in today's globalised world.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening maktabdagi eng sevimli fanim, albatta, ingliz tili. Men uni juda qiziqarli deb bilaman, chunki u juda ko'p imkoniyatlarga yo'l ochadi – xorijiy filmlarni tushunishdan tortib, butun dunyo bo'ylab odamlar bilan muloqot qilishgacha.

Menga uning ijodiy tomoni ham yoqadi, masalan, insholar yozish va yangi iboralarni o'rganish. Menimcha, bugungi globallashgan dunyoda ingliz tilini mukammal bilish juda muhim.

questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like English. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like English. I like to learn new words and I can talk to my teacher. But grammar is difficult.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like studying English. I think it's a very useful language to learn. For example, I can understand movies and songs better. However, sometimes it's difficult to remember all the vocabulary. But overall, I enjoy it.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, I genuinely do, although I'll admit it can be frustrating at times. The thing is, English opens so many doors for me — I can watch films, follow the news, and chat with people from all walks of life. I suppose the hardest part is getting to grips with all the grammar, but honestly, the benefits far outweigh the downsides.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men ingliz tilini yaxshi ko'raman. U yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga ingliz tili yoqadi. Men yangi so'zlarni o'rganishni yaxshi ko'raman va o'qituvchim bilan gaplasha olaman. Lekin grammatika qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menga ingliz tilini o'rganish yoqadi. Menimcha, bu o'rganish uchun juda foydali til.
Masalan, men filmlar va qo'shiqlarni yaxshiroq tushuna olaman.
Biroq, ba'zida barcha so'zlarni eslab qolish qiyin.
Lekin umuman olganda, menga bu yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men ingliz tilini o'rganishdan zavqlanaman, garchi ba'zida bu asabiylashishi mumkin. Turli madaniyatlardan bo'lgan odamlar bilan muloqot qila olish va menga boshqacha tarzda mavjud bo'lmaydigan ma'lumotlarga kirish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lish juda foydali deb bilaman. Bu, albatta, qiyin, ayniqsa tilning yanada nozik jihatlarini o'zlashtirishga kelganda, lekin menimcha, foydalari qiyinchiliklardan ancha ustun turadi.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you like studying English?
idioms: Rome wasn't built in a day - "Rim bir kunda qurilmagan"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I genuinely enjoy studying…" - "Ha, men haqiqatan ham … o'rganishni yoqtiraman"
"Of course, some aspects can be challenging…" - "Albatta, ba'zi tomonlari qiyin bo'lishi mumkin…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I genuinely enjoy studying English. It's not just a school subject for me — it's a skill that I use in my everyday life, whether I'm watching YouTube videos, reading articles online, or chatting with friends from other countries.
Of course, some aspects can be challenging, like mastering grammar rules, but I think the sense of achievement you get when you successfully express yourself in another language makes it all worth the effort.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men ingliz tilini o'rganishdan chin dildan zavqlanaman. Bu men uchun shunchaki maktab predmeti emas — bu men kundalik hayotimda ishlatadigan ko'nikma, xoh YouTube videolarini tomosha qilaymi, xoh internetda maqolalar o'qiymanmi, yoki boshqa davlatlardan kelgan do'stlarim bilan suhbatlashamanmi.

Albatta, ba'zi jihatlari qiyin bo'lishi mumkin, masalan, grammatika qoidalarini o'zlashtirish, lekin menimcha, o'zingizni boshqa tilda muvaffaqiyatli ifoda etganingizda oladigan yutuq hissi barcha sa'y-harakatlarga arziydi.

questions.prompt: Do you like mornings or evenings?
questions.sampleA2:
I like evenings.

Because I can watch TV.

And I can sleep late.
questions.sampleB1:
Well, I prefer evenings.

I think mornings are difficult for me.

I am not a morning person.

In the evening, I can relax and do things I like.

For example, watch movies or read a book.
questions.sampleB2: I'd say I'm much more of an evening person, to be honest. Mornings tend to be a bit of a rush — I'm half asleep and it takes me ages to get going. Evenings, on the other hand, are when I really come alive. Once things quieten down, I can unwind, catch up on my hobbies, and just enjoy some peace and quiet.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga kechqurunlar yoqadi.

Chunki men televizor ko'rishim mumkin.

Va men kech uxlashim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, men kechqurunlarni afzal ko'raman.

O'ylashimcha, ertalablar men uchun qiyin.

Men ertalabki odam emasman.

Kechqurun men dam olib, o'zimga yoqqan ishlarni qila olaman.

Masalan, kino ko'rish yoki kitob o'qish.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men, albatta, kechqurunlarni afzal ko'raman.

Ertalablar odatda shoshilish bilan o'tadi, ish boshlashdan oldin hamma narsani tugatishga harakat qilasiz.

Kechqurunlar esa, dam olish va shaxsiy qiziqishlaringiz bilan shug'ullanish imkoniyatini beradi.

Men sokinlikni va vaqtimni qanday o'tkazishni tanlash erkinligini qadrlayman.

Qolaversa, men kechqurun soatlarida, chalg'itadigan narsalar kamroq bo'lganda, ko'proq ijodiy va diqqatli bo'laman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you like mornings or evenings?
idioms: different strokes for different folks - "har kimning o'z didi bor"
the early bird catches the worm - "erta turgan kishi – baxtli kishi"
phrases: get into the swing of things - "ishga kirishib ketmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say I'm more of an evening person…" - "Menimcha, men ko'proq kechqurunchi odamman…"
"Evenings, on the other hand, are when…" - "Kechqurun esa, aksincha, …"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say I'm more of an evening person, to be honest. In the mornings, I tend to feel a bit sluggish and it takes me a while to get into the swing of things.
Evenings, on the other hand, are when I feel most genuinely productive and creative. I enjoy the calm atmosphere after a busy day — it's the perfect time to study, read, or just unwind and relax. As they say, "different strokes for different folks".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men ko'proq kechki odamman desam bo'ladi. Ertalab men biroz dangasalik his qilaman va ishga kirishishim uchun biroz vaqt kerak bo'ladi.

Kechqurunlari esa, o'zimni eng chinakam samarali va ijodiy his qilaman. Band kunimdan keyingi sokin muhit menga yoqadi — bu o'qish, kitob o'qish yoki shunchaki dam olish uchun ajoyib vaqt. Aytishlaricha, "har kimning o'z didi bor".

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA2: I see a boy with his family. They are smiling. And I see kids playing outside, and they are happy because they are with friends.
questions.sampleB1: In the first picture, I see a family. They are doing something together, maybe a game. It looks like they are having fun. In the second picture, there are some kids playing. I think they are friends. They are also smiling, so I guess they are enjoying themselves.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can see a family – a mother, father, and their young son – sitting on the floor in what appears to be their living room. They're fully engrossed in a game of Jenga, carefully taking turns to remove blocks. Everyone seems quite content and focused on the game, enjoying some quality time together. The second image also features children gathered around a table, playing Jenga. Their expressions are similarly animated, showing excitement and concentration as they try to keep the tower from falling. Overall, both pictures highlight the joy and engagement of playing traditional board games indoors.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men bir bola va uning oilasini ko'ryapman. Ular kulishmoqda. Va men tashqarida o'ynayotgan bolalarni ko'ryapman, va ular xursand, chunki ular do'stlari bilan birga.
questions.uzSampleB1: Birinchi rasmda men bir oilani ko'ryapman. Ular birgalikda nimadir qilishyapti, balki o'yin o'ynashayotgandir. Ularning kayfiyati yaxshi ko'rinadi. Ikkinchi rasmda esa, bir nechta bolalar o'ynashyapti. Menimcha, ular do'stlar. Ular ham kulishayapti, shuning uchun menimcha, ular ham zavqlanishyapti.
questions.uzSampleB2: Birinchi rasmda bola o'z oilasi bilan muloqot qilayotganini ko'rish mumkin, ehtimol ular stol o'yini yoki boshqa bir faoliyat bilan shug'ullanmoqda. Atmosfera juda ijobiy va qo'llab-quvvatlovchi ko'rinadi. Ikkinchi rasmda bola boshqa bolalar bilan o'ynayapti, taxminan do'stlari bilan. Bu yanada faol va tashqi tomondan ifodaliroq muloqot ekanligi ko'rinadi. Ikkala rasm ham, shunga qaramay, bolalarning rivojlanishi uchun ijtimoiy aloqalarning muhimligini ta'kidlaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: blood is thicker than water - "qon suvdan quyuq (oila eng muhim)"
a friend in need is a friend indeed - "haqiqiy do'st — boshingga mushkul tushganda bilinar"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see…" - "Birinchi rasmda men ko'ryapman…"
"The contrast between the two…" - "Ikkalasi orasidagi farq…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see a child spending quality time with family members. They appear to be happily engaged in an activity together, which creates a warm and loving atmosphere.
In the second picture, a child is playing with friends, and they seem to be having a lot of fun. The contrast between the two images highlights how children benefit from both family bonding and peer interaction in different ways.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda men bir bolani oila a'zolari bilan sifatli vaqt o'tkazayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Ular birgalikda biror faoliyat bilan xursandchilik bilan mashg'ul bo'lib, iliq va mehrga to'la muhit yaratayotganga o'xshaydi.

Ikkinchi rasmda bir bola do'stlari bilan o'ynayapti va ular juda xursand bo'lishayotganga o'xshaydi. Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq bolalar oilaviy rishtalardan ham, tengdoshlar bilan muloqotdan ham har xil yo'llar bilan qanday foyda olishini ta'kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Why do children need to spend time with their family?
questions.sampleA1: Family is good. I like my family. We play. I am happy.
questions.sampleA2: I like my family. We eat dinner together and it is fun. I think it is important because they help me. And I love them.
questions.sampleB1: I think children need to spend time with their family because it's important for them. For example, they can learn many things from their parents and siblings. Also, spending time together makes the family closer. In my opinion, it helps children grow up to be good people.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I'd say family time is absolutely vital for a child's development. First and foremost, it gives them a real sense of security — they feel loved and supported no matter what. On top of that, it's within the family that kids pick up core values like respect and kindness. To my mind, those early bonds shape the kind of person they'll grow into.
questions.uzSampleA1: Oila yaxshi. Men oilamni yaxshi ko'raman. Biz o'ynaymiz. Men xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men oilamni yaxshi ko'raman. Biz birga kechki ovqat yeymiz va bu qiziqarli. Menimcha, bu muhim, chunki ular menga yordam berishadi. Va men ularni sevaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, bolalar oilasi bilan vaqt o'tkazishi kerak, chunki bu ular uchun muhim.
Masalan, ular ota-onalari va aka-ukalaridan ko'p narsalarni o'rganishlari mumkin. Shuningdek, birga vaqt o'tkazish oilani yanada yaqinlashtiradi.
Mening fikrimcha, bu bolalarga yaxshi inson bo'lib ulg'ayishga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bolalar uchun oila bilan vaqt o'tkazish bir necha sabablarga ko'ra juda muhim. Birinchidan, bu ularning hissiy farovonligi uchun zarur bo'lgan mansublik va xavfsizlik hissini uyg'otadi. Oila a'zolarining o'zaro munosabatlari bolalarga muhim ijtimoiy ko'nikmalar va qadriyatlarni o'rganish imkoniyatini beradi. Bundan tashqari, bu umumiy tajribalar uzoq muddatli xotiralarni yaratadi va oilaviy rishtalarni mustahkamlaydi, bu esa bolaning rivojlanishi uchun qo'llab-quvvatlovchi va barqaror muhitga hissa qo'shadi.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Why do children need to spend time with their family?
idioms: like father, like son - "otasini ko'rib o'g'il o'sar"
sentenceStarters: "I believe spending time with family is absolutely…" - "Menimcha, oila bilan vaqt o'tkazish mutlaqo…"
"First and foremost, family provides…" - "Eng avvalo, oila ta'minlaydi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I believe spending time with family is absolutely essential for a child's development. First and foremost, family provides a sense of security and emotional support that children need to feel confident and loved.
When children spend time with their parents and siblings, they learn core values such as respect, responsibility, and kindness — lessons that are rarely taught as effectively anywhere else. Family time also strengthens emotional bonds, which helps children develop better communication skills and a healthier sense of self.
Moreover, shared activities like cooking, playing games, or simply having dinner together create lasting memories and build trust. As the saying goes, "charity begins at home" — the values and habits formed within the family shape who we become as adults.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, oila bilan vaqt o'tkazish bolaning rivojlanishi uchun mutlaqo zarur. Birinchi navbatda, oila bolalarga o'zlarini ishonchli va sevgi his qilishlari uchun zarur bo'lgan xavfsizlik hissi va hissiy qo'llab-quvvatlashni ta'minlaydi.

Bolalar ota-onalari va aka-ukalari bilan vaqt o'tkazganda, ular hurmat, mas'uliyat va mehribonlik kabi asosiy qadriyatlarni o'rganadilar - bu darslar boshqa joyda kamdan-kam hollarda shu qadar samarali o'rgatiladi. Oila bilan vaqt o'tkazish, shuningdek, hissiy aloqalarni mustahkamlaydi, bu bolalarga yaxshiroq muloqot qilish qobiliyatlarini va sog'lomroq o'zlik hissini rivojlantirishga yordam beradi.

Bundan tashqari, ovqat pishirish, o'yin o'ynash yoki shunchaki birga kechki ovqat qilish kabi umumiy mashg'ulotlar unutilmas xotiralarni yaratadi va ishonchni mustahkamlaydi. Aytishlaricha, "yaxshilik uyidan boshlanadi" - oila ichida shakllangan qadriyatlar va odatlar bizning kattalar sifatida kim bo'lishimizni belgilaydi.

questions.prompt: Why do many children like spending time with friends?
questions.sampleA1: I like friends. Friends are fun. We play. I am happy.
questions.sampleA2: I like to play with my friends because it is fun. We play games and we laugh. Sometimes we argue, but we are still friends. My friends are important to me.
questions.sampleB1: I think children like spending time with their friends because it's enjoyable. For example, they can play games together and have fun. Also, friends understand each other and they can talk about things they like. In my opinion, it's important for children to have friends.
questions.sampleB2: Kids are naturally drawn to their friends because that's where they feel they belong. With friends, they can let their hair down and be themselves, without the rules that come with home life. On top of that, playing together teaches them to share, take turns, and sort out disagreements. At the end of the day, friendships bring a kind of fun that's hard to beat.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men do'stlarni yaxshi ko'raman. Do'stlar bilan qiziqarli. Biz o'ynaymiz. Men xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'stlarim bilan o'ynashni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki bu qiziqarli. Biz o'yinlar o'ynaymiz va kulamiz. Ba'zida biz tortishamiz, lekin biz baribir do'stmiz. Do'stlarim men uchun muhim.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, bolalar do'stlari bilan vaqt o'tkazishni yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki bu yoqimli.
Masalan, ular birgalikda o'yinlar o'ynashlari va xursand bo'lishlari mumkin. Shuningdek, do'stlar bir-birini tushunishadi va ular o'zlari yoqtirgan narsalar haqida gaplashishlari mumkin.
Mening fikrimcha, bolalar uchun do'stlar bo'lishi muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bolalar ko'pincha do'stlari bilan vaqt o'tkazishni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki ularda ijtimoiy aloqaga bo'lgan tabiiy ehtiyoj bor. Ular o'rtoqlik va umumiy tajriba tuyg'usini topadilar, bu juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, do'stlik bolalarga hamkorlik va hamdardlik kabi muhim ijtimoiy ko'nikmalarni rivojlantirishga imkon beradi, bu ularning umumiy rivojlanishi uchun juda muhimdir. Bu, shuningdek, ular oilaviy muhitdan tashqarida o'z shaxsiyatlari va qiziqishlarini o'rganishlari, mustaqillik va o'z-o'zini kashf etishni rivojlantirishlari mumkin bo'lgan joydir.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do many children like spending time with friends?
idioms: no man is an island - "hech kim orol emas (hamma bir-biriga muhtoj)"
birds of a feather flock together - "o'xshash odamlar birlashadi"
phrases: belonging and acceptance - "tegishlilik va qabul qilinish hissi"
sentenceStarters: "There are several reasons why children are naturally…" - "Bolalarning tabiiy ravishda … bir nechta sabablari bor"
"Friends also offer something that family sometimes can't…" - "Do'stlar ba'zan oila bera olmaydigan narsani taqdim etadi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why children are naturally drawn to spending time with their friends. The most important one is the sense of belonging and acceptance — children want to feel that they fit in and are valued by their peers.
Friends also offer something that family sometimes can't — a space where children feel free to be themselves without the rules and expectations that come with home life. Playing with friends helps develop social skills like teamwork, negotiation, and conflict resolution, which are incredibly important later in life.
Additionally, friendships bring fun and excitement — children genuinely enjoy sharing experiences, discovering new games, and building their own little world. As they say, "no man is an island" — we all need meaningful connections with others, and for children, friendships are the first step towards that.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bolalarning do'stlari bilan vaqt o'tkazishga intilishining bir nechta sabablari bor. Eng muhimi, mansublik va qabul qilinish hissi – bolalar o'zlarini moslashgan va tengdoshlari tomonidan qadrlangan his qilishni xohlashadi.

Do'stlar, shuningdek, oila ba'zan bera olmaydigan narsani taklif qilishadi – bolalar uy hayoti bilan birga keladigan qoidalar va umidlarsiz, o'zlarini erkin his qiladigan joy. Do'stlar bilan o'ynash jamoaviy ish, muzokaralar va nizolarni hal qilish kabi ijtimoiy ko'nikmalarni rivojlantirishga yordam beradi, bu esa keyingi hayotda juda muhimdir.

Bundan tashqari, do'stlik quvonch va hayajon olib keladi – bolalar tajribalarni baham ko'rishdan, yangi o'yinlarni kashf qilishdan va o'z kichik dunyosini qurishdan chinakam zavqlanishadi. Aytishlaricha, "hech kim orol emas" – hammamizga boshqalar bilan mazmunli aloqalar kerak va bolalar uchun do'stliklar shu tomonga qo'yilgan birinchi qadamdir.

questions.prompt: Describe a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
questions.sampleA1: I make mistake. I forget homework. Teacher angry. Now I remember.
questions.sampleA2: I made a mistake. I lost my keys. I was very sad and my mom was angry. But I found them later and now I put them in my bag.
questions.sampleB1: Okay, so I remember one time I made a mistake. I forgot to send an important email for my job. I didn't write it down, and I just forgot. My boss was not very happy. However, I learned that I need to write everything down so I don't forget. I think it was a good lesson for me.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so I'd like to talk about a mistake I made a couple of years ago, back when I was getting ready for a really important exam. To be honest, it still makes me cringe a little when I think about it. Instead of buckling down and starting my revision early, I kept putting it off, telling myself I could cram everything into one last weekend. Big mistake. When the exam came around, my mind went blank and I ended up scraping a pass by the skin of my teeth. At first, I was gutted and pretty hard on myself. But rather than dwelling on it, I decided to take a step back and figure out where I'd gone wrong. The thing is, I realised the problem wasn't that I wasn't clever enough — it was that I'd left everything to the last minute. So I sat down and drew up a proper study plan, breaking the material into small chunks and chipping away at it day by day. Second time round, I sailed through with a much better grade. Looking back, I suppose that slip-up taught me a lesson I'll never forget. Nowadays, I always plan ahead and never bite off more than I can chew. Whenever I take on a big project, I break it down into manageable steps instead of leaving it all until the eleventh hour. As they say, failing to prepare is preparing to fail — and honestly, that little setback turned out to be one of the best things that could have happened to me.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men xato qildim. Men uyga vazifani unutdim. O'qituvchi jahli chiqdi. Endi eslayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men xato qildim. Men kalitlarimni yo'qotib qo'ydim. Men juda xafa bo'ldim va onam jahli chiqdi. Lekin men ularni keyinroq topdim va endi ularni sumkamga solib qo'yaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, men bir marta xato qilganim esimda. Men ishim uchun muhim elektron pochta xabarini yuborishni unutdim. Men uni yozib qo'ymadim va shunchaki unutib qo'ydim. Boshlig'im unchalik xursand bo'lmadi.
Shunga qaramay, men hamma narsani yozib qo'yishim kerakligini, shunda unutmasligimni o'rgandim. O'ylaymanki, bu men uchun yaxshi saboq bo'ldi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Esimga kelgan xato shuki, men ishda loyihani tugatish uchun zarur bo'lgan vaqtni past baholaganman. Men menejerimga uni bir hafta ichida tugata olishimni aytdim, lekin men barcha zarur qadamlarni to'liq hisobga olmagan edim.

bo'lib tashlayman va muddatni belgilashdan oldin har birining vaqtini baholayman.

bulletPoints: Describe a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
What was the mistake and how did you deal with it?
How has this lesson influenced your decisions or behaviour since then?
questions.sampleAnswer:
The mistake I made:
I'd like to talk about a mistake I made a couple of years ago when I was preparing for an important exam. Instead of starting my revision early, I foolishly left everything to the last minute, thinking I could cram all the material in one weekend. Unsurprisingly, I didn't perform nearly as well as I had hoped.
How I dealt with it:
At first, I felt extremely disappointed in myself. However, instead of dwelling on the failure, I decided to take responsibility and learn from it. I created a proper study schedule for the retake and consistently followed it, dedicating a set number of hours each day to revision. This time, I passed with a much higher score and felt a real sense of accomplishment.
How it has influenced me since:
This experience profoundly changed my approach to work and deadlines. Now, I always plan ahead and break tasks down into manageable parts. I've learned that "failing to prepare is preparing to fail", and that mistakes are not the end of the world — they are our greatest teachers if we choose to learn from them.

Men qilgan xato:

Men bir necha yil oldin muhim imtihonga tayyorgarlik ko'rayotganimda qilgan xatom haqida gapirmoqchiman. Takrorlashni erta boshlash o'rniga, men hamma narsani oxirgi daqiqaga qoldirdim, butun materialni bir dam olish kunida siqib chiqaraman deb o'yladim. Ajablanarlisi yo'q, men o'ylaganchalik yaxshi natijaga erisha olmadim.

Men unga qanday munosabatda bo'ldim:

Dastlab, men o'zimdan juda xafa bo'ldim. Biroq, muvaffaqiyatsizlikka berilib ketish o'rniga, men mas'uliyatni o'z zimmamga olishga va undan saboq olishga qaror qildim. Men qayta topshirish uchun to'g'ri o'qish jadvalini tuzdim va unga doimiy ravishda amal qildim, har kuni takrorlashga ma'lum soatlar ajratdim. Bu safar men ancha yuqori ball bilan o'tdim va haqiqiy yutuq hissini tuydim.

Bu menga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Bu tajriba mening ishga va muddatlarga bo'lgan yondashuvimni tubdan o'zgartirdi. Endi men har doim oldindan rejalashtiraman va vazifalarni boshqarish mumkin bo'lgan qismlarga ajrataman. Men "tayyorgarlik ko'rmaslik - muvaffaqiyatsizlikka tayyorgarlik" ekanligini va xatolar dunyoning oxiri emasligini angladim - agar biz ulardan saboq olishni tanlasak, ular bizning eng buyuk o'qituvchilarimizdir.

questions.prompt: The use of Artificial Intelligence should be mandatory in schools.
questions.sampleA1: AI... school? I don't know. AI is computer. School... study. Maybe good?
questions.sampleA2: AI in schools... I think it's okay. It can help students, and teachers too. But maybe it's expensive, and some students don't have computers at home, so it's not fair for everyone.
questions.sampleB1: I think using AI in schools could be a good idea. For example, it might help students learn at their own pace. Also, it could help teachers with some of their work. However, I think it's important to make sure that all students have access to the technology and that teachers are properly trained to use it.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really hot topic these days, especially with technology creeping into every corner of our lives. On the one hand, I can see why people are all for making AI compulsory in schools. For starters, it can tailor lessons to each student, so nobody gets left behind or held back. It can also take a lot of the paperwork off teachers' plates, freeing them up to focus on what really matters — actually teaching. And let's face it, these kids are growing up in a world run by technology, so getting to grips with it early can only stand them in good stead. That said, I do have my reservations. If students lean on AI for everything, they might never learn to think for themselves, and that could really stifle their creativity, since the machine would essentially be doing all the hard thinking for them. There's also the thorny issue of data privacy — schools would be sitting on huge amounts of personal information. On top of that, making it mandatory could widen the gap between well-off schools and those that simply can't afford the technology. All things considered, I'd say AI definitely has a place in the classroom, but I wouldn't go so far as to make it compulsory. To my mind, it should be brought in gradually, as a handy tool that backs teachers up rather than replacing them. As the saying goes, technology is a good servant but a bad master, so we ought to keep the human touch at the heart of education.
questions.uzSampleA1: Sun'iy intellekt... maktab? Bilmayman. Sun'iy intellekt bu kompyuter. Maktab... o'qish. Balki yaxshidir?
questions.uzSampleA2: Maktablarda sun'iy intellekt... Menimcha, bu yaxshi. U o'quvchilarga ham, o'qituvchilarga ham yordam berishi mumkin. Lekin balki bu qimmatdir va ba'zi o'quvchilarning uyida kompyuterlari yo'q, shuning uchun bu hamma uchun adolatli emas.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, maktablarda sun'iy intellektdan foydalanish yaxshi fikr bo'lishi mumkin.
Masalan, bu o'quvchilarga o'z tezligida o'rganishga yordam berishi mumkin. Shuningdek, bu o'qituvchilarga ba'zi ishlarida yordam berishi mumkin.
Biroq, menimcha, barcha o'quvchilar texnologiyaga ega bo'lishini va o'qituvchilar undan foydalanish uchun to'g'ri o'qitilganligiga ishonch hosil qilish muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Sun'iy intellektni maktablarda majburiy qilish g'oyasi ham imkoniyatlar, ham qiyinchiliklarni taqdim etadi. Bir tomondan, AI ta'limni shaxsiylashtirishi, har bir o'quvchiga moslashtirilgan yordam taklif qilishi mumkin. Shuningdek, u ba'zi ma'muriy vazifalarni avtomatlashtirishi, o'qituvchilarning vaqtini tejash imkonini beradi.
Biroq, majburiy yondashuv ijodkorlikni va tanqidiy fikrlash qobiliyatlarini bo'g'ishi mumkin, chunki o'quvchilar AIga haddan tashqari bog'lanib qolishlari mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bunday siyosatni amalga oshirishdan oldin ehtiyotkorlik bilan hal qilinishi kerak bo'lgan ma'lumotlar maxfiyligi va texnologiyadan teng foydalanish bilan bog'liq axloqiy masalalar mavjud.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly relevant debate, especially as technology continues to reshape education. Proponents of mandatory AI in schools argue that it can provide personalised learning experiences, adapting to each student's strengths and weaknesses in real time. It can also significantly reduce the administrative burden on teachers, freeing them up to focus on actual teaching and mentoring.
However, opponents raise some valid concerns. Over-reliance on AI could potentially weaken students' critical thinking and creativity — if a machine does the thinking for you, you may never learn to think for yourself. There are also serious issues around data privacy, since schools would be collecting vast amounts of student information. Furthermore, making AI mandatory could widen the digital divide, as schools in poorer areas may simply lack the resources to implement such technology.
In my opinion, AI should be gradually integrated into education as a supportive tool rather than made compulsory. As the saying goes, "technology is a good servant but a bad master" — we should use it wisely without letting it replace the human element in teaching.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu juda dolzarb bahs, ayniqsa texnologiya ta'limni qayta shakllantirishda davom etar ekan. Maktablarda sun'iy intellektni majburiy qilish tarafdorlari, u har bir o'quvchining kuchli va zaif tomonlariga real vaqt rejimida moslashib, shaxsiy o'rganish tajribalarini taqdim etishi mumkinligini ta'kidlaydilar. Shuningdek, u o'qituvchilarning ma'muriy yukini sezilarli darajada kamaytirishi, ularga haqiqiy o'qitish va murabbiylikka e'tibor qaratishga imkon beradi.

Biroq, qarshilar ba'zi asosli xavotirlarni keltirib chiqarmoqdalar. Sun'iy intellektga haddan tashqari bog'lanish o'quvchilarning tanqidiy fikrlash va ijodkorlik qobiliyatini zaiflashtirishi mumkin - agar mashina siz uchun o'ylasa, siz hech qachon o'zingiz o'ylashni o'rganmasligingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, ma'lumotlar maxfiyligi bilan bog'liq jiddiy muammolar mavjud, chunki maktablar o'quvchilar haqida juda ko'p ma'lumot to'plashadi. Bundan tashqari, sun'iy intellektni majburiy qilish raqamli tafovutni kengaytirishi mumkin, chunki kambag'alroq hududlardagi maktablarda bunday texnologiyalarni joriy etish uchun resurslar yetishmasligi mumkin.

Mening fikrimcha, sun'iy intellekt majburiy qilinmasdan, balki qo'llab-quvvatlovchi vosita sifatida ta'limga asta-sekin integratsiya qilinishi kerak. Aytishlaricha, "texnologiya yaxshi xizmatkor, ammo yomon xo'jayin" - biz undan oqilona foydalanishimiz kerak, lekin unga o'qitishdagi insoniy elementni almashtirishga yo'l qo'ymasligimiz kerak.
